evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形 / 字樣說明 / 釋義
evidence.text: The entry attributes to Shuowen the analysis 从水，气聲, with glosses “water dried up” and alternatively “tears falling.” It reports a Jiyun gloss “water vapor” and says modern 汽 is used especially in compounds for water vapor and gasoline, while older meanings are now carried by 汔. It supplies no dates for these changes.
evidence.title: 汽 - 教育部《異體字字典》 臺灣學術網路十四版（正式七版）2024

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry repeats the Shuowen phonosemantic analysis: water is the semantic element and 气 the sound element, with the gloss “water dried up.” It reports the vapor gloss by citing Jiyun; this does not independently date the first vapor use.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 汽

evidence.text: Lists Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) Old Chinese *kʰɯds for both 汽 and 气. This within-system comparison is consistent with the sound-element analysis; it is secondary reconstruction evidence, not a dated record of the graph or its pronunciation.

search_audit.query: 汽 說文 从水 气聲 汽 小篆 字形
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Taiwan MOE and CUHK entries. zi.tools returned a JavaScript shell; Chinese Text Project returned 403. The inspected dictionary accounts support water as semantic element and 气 as sound element.
Search results showed the Xiaoxuetang database but no 汽-specific record or direct glyph image URL.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org 汽 seal script Chinese character
search_audit.outcome: Found and inspected the exact Commons file description in search output: 汽-seal.svg, described as a Shuowen seal-style vector and marked public domain. Opening the exact page returned a cache miss, and a follow-up search for its upload.wikimedia.org URL returned no results. An exact-filename redirect is available, but the original-file URL could not be verified.
No search results; original upload URL not independently established.
Both character-specific Unicode pages returned access errors; no official Unihan character record was inspected.

gaps: No directly inspected archaeological oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript form of 汽 was found. The available historical glyph candidate is a modern digital redraw in Shuowen seal-script style, not an artifact photograph.

The Shuowen glosses “water dried up” and “tears falling” and the later Jiyun-reported vapor gloss are documented separately, but the earliest attestation of the vapor sense and any semantic link remain undated or unestablished.
The report that 汔 now carries older meanings does not establish when or how that distribution arose. No evidence of graphic corruption was found.

Modern readings are qì for both 气 and 汽 in the supplied local Unihan rows. Their official character-specific Unihan pages were inaccessible. The local Baxter–Sagart table supplies 气 *C.qʰəp-s but no 汽 row; Zhengzhang *kʰɯds values must remain explicitly attributed to that separate system.

Commons search established an exact file page and reuse statement, but the exact page open failed with a cache miss and the original upload URL could not be verified. The image URL below uses the Commons redirect for the established exact filename.
